Elected to the Gujarat Legislative Assembly from Jamnagar North in 2022 as a BJP leader, this politician was later appointed a junior minister under the state's chief minister — who is she?
Born in England, she married the future first president of Botswana and went on to serve as that nation's inaugural First Lady from 1966 to 1980. Who was she?
Ruth Williams Khama: First Lady of Botswana from 1966 to 1980.

Originally referring to peoples near ancient Arabia, this medieval European term evolved after the rise of Islam into the standard Christian label for Muslims and the Muslim world broadly — what was the term?
Saracen: Archaic term for Arabs and later for all Muslims.
Pitting Britain and Prussia against France and Austria from 1756 to 1763, this global conflict was later dubbed the 'First World War' by Winston Churchill for its sheer scale — what was it called?
Seven Years' War: Global war among European powers (1756–1763)
Born into a wealthy Caracas family and nicknamed El Libertador, this military officer led six present-day South American nations to independence from Spain — who was he?
Simón Bolívar: Venezuelan statesman and military officer (1783–1830)

Honored with the title "Netaji," or "Respected Leader," this Indian anti-colonial figure became a hero for defying British rule — though his wartime alliances with the Axis left a troubled legacy. Who was he?
Subhas Chandra Bose: Indian nationalist leader (1897–1945)
This form of governance grounds legitimacy in scientific and technical expertise rather than the rule of the people — what's it called?
Technocracy: Form of government ruled by experts.

Governed by the Ganden Phodrang and declared independent by the 13th Dalai Lama after the Qing dynasty's collapse in 1912, this East Asian state was annexed by the People's Republic of China in 1951 — which state?
Tibet (1912–1951): Former de facto state in East Asia.
During the American Civil War, what was the name for the federal government and loyal states that refused to recognize the Confederacy after Lincoln's 1860 election?
Union (American Civil War): US federal government from 1861 to 1865.

Ruling for just eight months during the chaotic Year of the Four Emperors, this Roman ruler took the honorific Germanicus instead of Caesar and tried to boost his popularity by imitating the still-beloved Nero — who was he?
Carved out of the Carolingian Empire at the Treaty of Verdun in 843 and lasting until the Capetians took over in 987, which kingdom was the very first stage of what we now call France?
West Francia: Predecessor of France from 843 to 987.
The paramount leader of China since 2012, this politician served as general secretary of the Communist Party and was sent to a rural village as a teenager during the Cultural Revolution. Who is he?
Xi Jinping: Leader of China since 2012. Xi Jinping (born 15 June 1953) is a Chinese politician who is the paramount leader of China.
This Chinese politician led the Communist Party's anti-corruption watchdog from 2017 to 2022 before becoming chairman of the National People's Congress Standing Committee — who is he?
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Saint Valentine (born 175) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
Assembly language (founded 1949) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Who among these is a chemist?
Dmitri Mendeleev is a chemist. The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
What is the atomic number of Flerovium?
Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
What is the atomic number of Yttrium?
Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
In what year was Galileo Galilei born?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year was Anton Chekhov born?
Anton Chekhov: Along with Henrik Ibsen and August Strindberg, Chekhov is often referred to as one of the three seminal figures in the birth of early modernism in the theatre.
In what year was Max Weber born?
Max Weber: Born in Erfurt in 1864, Weber studied law and history in Berlin, Göttingen, and Heidelberg.
In what year did Gregor Mendel die?
Gregor Mendel: Mendel worked with seven characteristics of pea plants: plant height, pod shape and colour, seed shape and colour, and flower position and colour.
In what year did Adam Smith die?
Adam Smith: The work is notable for its contribution to economic theory, particularly in its exposition of the concept of absolute advantage.
In what year was Argon discovered?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Which company manufactures Consolidated B-24 Liberator?
Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control
Consolidated B-24 Liberator: North American Aviation. The Consolidated B-24 Liberator is an American heavy bomber, designed by Consolidated Aircraft of San Diego, California.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Circinus?
Circinus: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
Who is credited with discovering Citric acid?
Citric acid: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
Who is credited with discovering Helium?
Helium: Pierre Janssen. Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
Russell Crowe stars in this 2001 Ron Howard film about a Nobel Prize-winning mathematician's struggle with schizophrenia, based on Sylvia Nasar's biography. What's the title?
A Beautiful Mind (film) is a 2001 American biographical drama film about the mathematician John Nash who won a Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.
This French surgeon won the 1912 Nobel for pioneering vascular suturing, then teamed up with aviator Charles Lindbergh to build the first perfusion pump for organ transplantation. Who was he?
Alexis Carrel (28 June 1873 - 5 November 1944) was a French surgeon and biologist who spent most of his scientific career in the United States.
Dating back to the Neolithic Revolution around 13,000 BC, this branch of agriculture covers the breeding, feeding, and day-to-day care of livestock raised for meat, milk, or fiber — what's it called?
Animal husbandry is the branch of agriculture concerned with animals that are raised for meat, fibre, milk, or other products.
This American physicist won a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize for an effect, now bearing his name, that demonstrated light's particle nature — who was he?
Arthur Compton (September 10, 1892 - March 15, 1962) was an American physicist who shared the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics with C. T. R. Wilson.
Grown for its edible taproot in red or golden varieties and closely related to Swiss chard, this vegetable's leaves are eaten too, sold simply as "greens" — which root vegetable?
Beetroot is the taproot portion of a Beta vulgaris subsp.
Born as Hughes Helicopters' Model 77 to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles in a tandem cockpit — what is it?
Boeing AH-64 Apache (-) is an American twin-turboshaft attack helicopter with a tailwheel-type landing gear and a tandem cockpit for a crew of two.
This basic unit of digital information most often consists of eight bits, and is called an 'octet' in network protocol documents to avoid ambiguity. What is it?
Byte is a unit of digital information that most commonly consists of eight bits.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Besides identifying the laws of elastic collision, this Dutch polymath studied Saturn's rings and improved the design of the telescope — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens (14 April 1629 - 8 July 1695) was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, engineer, astronomer, and inventor who is regarded as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution.
Scholars still argue whether it merely transmits meaning or also creates it, but the simplest definition of this concept is the transmission of information — what is it?
Communication is commonly defined as the transmission of information.
Grown from tubers and known by the folk name 'sowbread,' this Primulaceae genus features flowers with distinctively upswept petals — which plant genus?
Cyclamen is a genus of 25 species of perennial flowering plants in the family Primulaceae.
This Russian chemist's great law let him predict three undiscovered elements — germanium, gallium, and scandium — and a synthetic element now bears his name; who was he?
Which American toy magnate teamed up with his wife Ruth to co-found Mattel and dream up Hot Wheels and Barbie?
Elliot Handler (April 9, 1916 - July 21, 2011) was an American inventor, business magnate, and the co-founder of Mattel.
Botanists use this word for any plant whose leaves stay green and functional through every season, never going bare like a deciduous tree — what is it?
Evergreen is a plant which has foliage that remains green and functional throughout the year.
Holding doctorates in both medicine and philosophy from Pisa by age 21, this Italian naturalist became the "founder of experimental biology" by disproving spontaneous generation — who was he?
Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 - 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.
The tallest living land animal and the largest ruminant on Earth, this African mammal's closest living relative is the shorter-necked okapi — name the animal?
Giraffe (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
This flatfish's English name blends words for 'holy' and 'flat fish,' a nod to its place on the Catholic holy-day menu. Which bottom-dwelling fish?
Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
Nesting monogamously in tree cavities across Africa, Asia, and Melanesia, these birds are unique for having their first two neck vertebrae fused solid — which birds?
Hornbill are birds found in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Melanesia of the family Bucerotidae.
Supplied by the lumbar spinal nerves and part of the femoral nerve, this fused pair of abdominal and thigh muscles is the body's strongest hip flexor — what is it called?
Iliopsoas (from Latin ile 'groin' and Ancient Greek (ps) 'muscles of the loins') refers to the joined psoas major and the iliacus muscles.
This condition causes a yellowish, sometimes greenish, tint to the skin and eyes due to high bilirubin levels, affecting an estimated 80% of babies in their first week of life — what is it called?
Jaundice is a yellowish or, less frequently, greenish pigmentation of the skin and sclera due to high bilirubin levels.

This American game show host and former software engineer won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004, the longest streak in its history, before becoming its host himself in 2021 — who is he?
Ken Jennings (born May 23, 1974) is an American game show host and author who has hosted the syndicated quiz show Jeopardy!
This Swiss polymath founded the study of graph theory and topology, and introduced much of modern mathematical notation, including the concept of a function — who is he?
Leonhard Euler (15 April 1707 - 18 September 1783) was a Swiss polymath who was active as a mathematician, physicist, astronomer, logician, geographer, music theorist and engineer.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran but long grown in Europe, this herb's leaves, roots, and seeds are all used in cooking, tasting like a more intense mix of celery and parsley — what is it?
Lovage (Levisticum officinale) is a perennial plant, the sole species in the genus Levisticum in the family Apiaceae, subfamily Apioideae.
Cold-sensitive and tasting of sweet pine and citrus, this kitchen herb is so close to its cousin that in parts of the Middle East the two names are used interchangeably with oregano. What is it?
Connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum to the pons, this brainstem structure plays a role in vision, hearing, and staying alert -- what is it called?
Midbrain is the uppermost portion of the brainstem connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum with the pons.
This semiaquatic rodent can stay submerged for up to seventeen minutes, propelled mainly by its webbed hind feet while its long, scaly tail helps steer — what animal is it?
Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
First isolated by Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford, which group-15 nonmetal with atomic number 7 is the most abundant species in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Usually caused by bacteria and sometimes requiring amputation in severe cases, this infectious inflammation of bone can be acute or chronic — which condition?
Osteomyelitis (OM) is the infectious inflammation of bone. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
Confirming and popularizing Isaac Newton's work, this French scholar authored the five-volume 'Mécanique céleste' and helped pioneer the Bayesian view of probability — who is he?

Pierre-Simon Laplace (23 March 1749 - 5 March 1827) was a French polymath, a scholar whose work has been instrumental in the fields of physics, astronomy, mathematics, engineering, statistics, and philosophy.
This chemical compound, known in nature as the mineral niter and historically as a form of saltpetre, is widely used in fertilizers. What is it?
Potassium nitrate is a chemical compound with a sharp, salty, bitter taste and the chemical formula KNO3.
Powered by a supermassive black hole accreting gas at its center, this extremely luminous type of galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy thousands of times over. What is it?
Quasar is an extremely luminous active galactic nucleus (AGN).
With Patrick Steptoe and Jean Purdy, this British physiologist pioneered the technique that led to the 1978 birth of Louise Brown, earning a 2010 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Robert Edwards (physiologist) (27 September 1925 - 10 April 2013) was a British physiologist and pioneer in reproductive medicine, and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) in particular.

Often striking suddenly after heavy lifting and described as a shooting pain down one leg, about 90% of cases trace to a spinal disc herniation pressing on a nerve root — what's this condition called?
Sciatica is pain going down the leg from the lower back.
This spiny thistle species has distinctive red-to-purple flowers and shiny, pale green mottled leaves, and is a fairly typical member of the daisy family — what plant is it?
Silybum marianum is a species of thistle.
This Polish-American Manhattan Project mathematician dreamed up the Monte Carlo method, the cellular automaton, and the design behind thermonuclear weapons — who was he?
Stanisław Ulam (13 April 1909 - 13 May 1984) was a Polish and, later an American mathematician who made important contributions in advancing the understanding of nuclear physics and computer science.

A leguminous tree bearing edible brown pod-like fruits with sweet, tangy pulp, indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia, its wood and seed oil have varied uses from cuisine to traditional medicine. What is this tree?
Tamarind (Tamarindus indica) is a leguminous tree bearing edible fruit that is indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia.
This herb is also called common thyme or garden thyme and belongs to the mint family, Lamiaceae — which species is it?
Thymus vulgaris (common thyme, German thyme, garden thyme or just thyme) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
Named from the Greek word for 'cheese' after being first isolated from milk protein in 1846, this standard amino acid is more water-loving than its close relative phenylalanine. Name the amino acid?
Tyrosine (symbol Tyr or Y) or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 20 standard amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins.

In physics, this phenomenon occurs when two coherent waves combine according to their phase difference, producing either a boosted 'constructive' amplitude or a canceling 'destructive' one — what's the effect called?
Wave interference is a phenomenon in which two coherent waves are combined by adding their intensities or displacements with due consideration for their phase difference.

Released from prison in June 2025 to resume leading Turkey's nationalist Victory Party, this politician previously served as deputy leader of the far-right Nationalist Movement Party in the mid-2010s — who is he?
Ümit Özdağ (born 3 March 1961) is a Turkish politician who returned to his position as the current leader of the Victory Party after being released from prison on 17 June 2025.
Nicknamed for the stripes on its legs and body, this day-biting mosquito native to Southeast Asia spreads dengue, yellow fever, and Chikungunya — what is it called?
Aedes albopictus: Species of mosquito. The insect is called a tiger mosquito as it has stripes, as does a tiger.
This diverse group of photosynthetic organisms ranges from microscopic plankton to seaweeds 50 metres long — yet excludes the land plants entirely. What is it?
Algae: Diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. Algae (AL-jee, UK also AL-ghee; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.
Critically endangered with barely two dozen wild individuals estimated in 2007, this big cat subspecies survives along the Russian-Chinese border in the Primorye region — which spotted predator?
Amur leopard: Subspecies of large cat. The Amur leopard (Panthera pardus orientalis) is a leopard subspecies native to the Primorye region of southeastern Russia and northern China.
This external body opening at the end of the digestive tract, positioned opposite the mouth, lets gas and solid waste pass out after digestion?
Anus: Digestive tract waste expulsion opening. Passage of feces through the anus is typically controlled by muscular sphincters, and failure to stop unwanted passages results in fecal incontinence.
Ranking as the second-largest lizard species after the Komodo dragon, this excellent swimmer thrives in lakes, rivers, and even city sewers across South and Southeast Asia — what is it?
Asian water monitor: Species of lizard. The Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
As the largest member of the grass family, one species of this plant can grow stalks over 46 meters tall and 36 centimeters thick — name the plant?
Bamboo: Subfamily of plants in the grass family.
Coined in 1814 by chemist William Hyde Wollaston, this polyatomic anion forms when carbonic acid loses a proton and plays a crucial role buffering the body's pH — what is it?
Bicarbonate: Polyatomic anion. It is a polyatomic anion with the chemical formula HCO−3.
Named in allusion to a 'Flying Fortress' that came before it, this pressurized WWII heavy bomber dropped the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Which aircraft?
Air warfare of World War II
Boeing B-29 Superfortress: US heavy bomber aircraft, 1942.
Nicknamed 'angel's trumpets' for its pendulous, fragrant blooms, this toxic nightshade-family genus is officially Extinct in the Wild yet thrives worldwide as a garden plant — which genus?
Brugmansia: Genus of flowering plants in the nightshade family.
Present in the gut or mouth of up to 60 percent of healthy adults, this opportunistic yeast turns dangerous in immunocompromised patients, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans: Species of fungus. Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
Named after a Louisiana parish and named the state's official canine in 1979, this herding breed was traditionally used to hunt feral boars — what breed is it?
Catahoula Leopard Dog: American breed of dog.
Known as lamb's quarters, goosefoot, or fat-hen, this fast-growing annual weed in the amaranth family is sometimes cultivated as food elsewhere — which plant?
Chenopodium album: Species of flowering plant in the goosefoot family.
This lincosamide antibiotic treats infections from strep throat to acne, but raises the risk of a specific gut infection roughly fourfold — what is it?
Clindamycin: Antibiotic. It can also be used to treat acne, and some cases of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
Best known for its powerful, beautiful song, this small Old World flycatcher sometimes hybridizes with a closely related thrush species where their ranges overlap — which bird?
Common nightingale: Species of bird. Its range partly overlaps with that of the more northerly thrush nightingale (Luscinia luscinia), a closely related species with which hybrids have occurred.
Also known as hawthorn, quickthorn, or May-tree, this genus of several hundred shrub and tree species in the rose family is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Crataegus: Genus of flowering plants in the rose family Rosaceae.

Developed as a successor to an earlier delta-wing fighter family, this French all-weather interceptor entered service with the French Air Force in 1974, equipped with Cyrano IV radar — what aircraft is it?
Dassault Mirage F1: French attack aircraft. During the 1960s, Dassault commenced development of what would become the Mirage F1 as a private venture, alongside the larger Mirage F2.
Native to North Africa and West Asia, this annual herb in the celery family lends its leaves and seeds as both an herb and a spice — what is it?
Dill: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.

This medical term covers abnormal cell or organ growth — from hip conditions to bone marrow disorders — and is generally distinguished from cancerous neoplasia, though some forms are precancerous. What is it called?
Dysplasia: Abnormal development, at macroscopic or microscopical level.
Australia's tallest native bird, this flightless species can sprint up to 48 kilometers per hour and often goes weeks without drinking water — which bird?
Emu: Large flightless bird endemic to Australia.
Every animal, plant, fungus and seaweed belongs to this domain, defined by one shared cellular feature: a nucleus wrapped in its own membrane. What are they called?
Eukaryote: Domain of life whose cells have nuclei.
This Stanford computer scientist built ImageNet, the vast labeled dataset that ignited the deep-learning revolution in computer vision in the 2010s. Who is she?
Also called vitamin B9, this essential nutrient the body can't make itself is vital for building DNA and RNA — which is why its synthetic form, folic acid, is added to fortified foods. What is it?
Folate: Vitamin B9; nutrient essential for DNA synthesis. Folate, also known as vitamin B9 and folacin, is one of the B vitamins.
Also known as reishi or lingzhi, this red-colored fungus grows on decaying hardwood in parts of Europe and China — what is it?

Inducted into the U.S. Air Force Hall of Fame in 2018, this American mathematician modeled the precise shape of the Earth — work later baked into the Global Positioning System that now guides your phone. Who is she?
Rising from the ashes of the cancelled F-111B, which variable-sweep-wing Navy fighter first flew in 1970 and deployed aboard USS Enterprise?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat: Carrier-based multi-role fighter aircraft family.
A 1930s-40s Hollywood star of films like Algiers, she also co-invented a radio guidance system during WWII — which glamorous on-screen inventor was she?
Hedy Lamarr: Austrian-American actress and inventor (1914–2000)
Known as the great apes, this primate family holds eight living species across four genera — orangutans, gorillas, chimps and bonobos, plus one more: us. What is it?
Hominidae: Family of primates. The original meaning of "hominid" referred only to humans (Homo) and their closest extinct relatives.
It usually causes no symptoms at all, yet this persistently elevated arterial pressure is a leading cause of stroke, heart failure and premature death worldwide — what's the medical name for it?
Hypertension: Long-term high blood pressure in the arteries.
This sleep disorder makes it hard to fall or stay asleep, leaving daytime drowsiness, irritability and trouble focusing in its wake — what's its clinical name?
Insomnia: Disorder causing trouble with sleeping.
This U.S. Marine Corps test pilot commanded SpaceX's Crew-7 mission and served as a flight engineer aboard the ISS during Expedition 69/70 — who is she?
Jasmin Moghbeli: NASA astronaut and US Marine Corps officer and test pilot (born 1983)
A 1983 MacArthur Fellow, this American mathematician's work on Hilbert's tenth problem proved crucial to its eventual resolution — now known as the MRDP theorem. Who was she?
Native to southern China and roughly the size of a large olive, which citrus fruit closely resembles a tiny orange and is famously cold-hardy?
Kumquat: Species of small fruit-bearing tree.
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Normally solitary and harmless, these short-horned grasshoppers can undergo a serotonin-triggered shift into gregarious swarming behavior under drought-then-growth conditions — what are they called?
Locust: Grasshopper that has a swarming phase.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).

Belonging to the ancient order Ephemeroptera and keeping primitive traits like long tails and wings that won't fold flat, which aquatic insect's water-dwelling nymphs signal a clean, unpolluted stream?
Mayfly: Aquatic insects of the order Ephemeroptera. Over 3,000 species of mayfly are known worldwide, grouped into over 400 genera in 42 families.
This colorless gas, made by swapping one hydrogen atom in ammonia for a methyl group, has a strong rotten-fish smell and serves as a building block for many compounds — what is it?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.

Named for being quieter than its relatives, this large white waterfowl carries an orange beak topped with a black knob that's bigger in males, and is more common in North America than in its native Europe — which bird?
Mute swan: Large species of waterfowl. The mute swan (Cygnus olor) is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order.
Also known in everyday speech as 'brain surgery,' this medical specialty treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and the entire nervous system — what is it called?
Neurosurgery: Medical specialty of disorders which affect any portion of the nervous system.
Named for a discredited belief that it 'rows' itself with its pelvic fins, this family of long pelagic fish includes the longest bony fish alive at up to 8 meters?
Oarfish: Pelagic lampriform fish belonging to Regalecidae.
Working alongside Lise Meitner and Fritz Strassmann in 1938, this German chemist co-discovered nuclear fission and later won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alone — who is he?
Otto Hahn: German nuclear chemist and Nobel laureate (1879–1968)

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Members of this eukaryotic kingdom mostly make their own food with chlorophyll, though parasitic kinds have ditched photosynthesis entirely to feed off others — what kingdom is it?
Plant: Kingdom of organisms. Historically, as in Aristotle's biology, the plant kingdom encompassed all living things that were not animals, and included algae and fungi.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
Excess fluid pooling in the lungs' air sacs impairs oxygen exchange and can be triggered by either heart failure or a range of unrelated causes — what condition is this?
Pulmonary edema: Fluid accumulation in the tissue and air spaces of the lungs.
This bird of prey, related to eagles and buzzards, now breeds only in Europe but has wandered as far as Finland and the Gambia — what raptor is it?
Red kite: Species of bird. The red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
Defined by a single pair of ever-growing incisors in each jaw, this mammalian order makes up about 40 percent of all mammal species — which order?
Rodent: Order of mammals. The rodent fossil record dates back to the Paleocene of Asia.
Commonly known as elder, with its blossoms called elderflower and its fruit elderberry, this genus contains between 20 and 30 flowering plant species — which genus?

Triggered when the body's own dysregulated response to infection starts damaging its tissues and organs, this life-threatening condition brings fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — which condition?

Sepsis: Life-threatening response to infection. Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.

This informal name applies to any shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc — a body plan that evolved independently many times through convergent evolution across unrelated lineages. What creature is it?
Slug: Shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc. Slug or land slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.

Numbering more than 9,000 species, these tiny hexapods are no longer classified as true insects and get their scientific class name from Greek words meaning 'glue' and 'peg,' after a structure called the collophore — what are they called?
Known in antiquity as 'oil of vitriol,' this odorless, syrupy liquid is so thirsty for water that it never occurs pure in nature and will char nearly anything it touches — which substance is it?
Prized for its durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood with a leather-like smell when freshly milled is a top choice for boat building — what is it?
Teak: Tree species native to South and Southeast Asia.
Colored metallic blue on top and silvery below for camouflage, this genus of warm-blooded ocean fish includes the giant Atlantic bluefin and eight of the true tuna species — what genus is it?
Thunnus: Genus of fishes. Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Known as a noxious weed for its spiky, woody burs that can puncture bare feet and even bicycle tires, this invasive desert-loving plant is native to Eurasia and Africa — name the species?
Tribulus terrestris: Species of flowering plant. Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
